experiment.plan: Arm every live collector on Core and the Minion, run for five 300 s collection cycles, then finalize. Fleet held at 5,250 devices, the failing rung of the pool-200 knee search (5,000 passed). netem delay 75ms 25ms on netsim enp6s19, so 50-100 ms uniform per PDU. Collectd threads=200, all busy for the whole window. The pool completes ~62,960 services/h against 63,048 required, so the pending queue floor grows ~85/h; at arming it had been growing for 8 h since the knee search ended (floor 13 -> 592). GC logging was enabled at runtime with jcmd VM.log because neither JVM is started with -Xlog, so the GC logs are pulled separately from /var/tmp/gclog.
experiment.question: What are Core and the Minion actually doing over five collection cycles at the 200-thread knee, 5,250 devices with 50-100 ms per SNMP PDU?

host.cpu: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2650 v4 @ 2.20GHz, 8 cores

sut.config_delta: collectd-configuration.xml: threads 50 -> 200 (the pool-sweep result; stock is 50, the earlier captures ran 100). Kafka exclusive forwarding (forward.metrics=true, metricTopic=metrics, EmptyResourceStorageDao, no local time-series store). Thresholding disabled. Database connection pool 50 -> 250. JAVA_HEAP_SIZE 10240, so -Xms8192m -Xmx10240m on OpenJDK 21.0.12 with G1GC. -XX:NativeMemoryTracking=summary in opennms.conf and MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4 via the systemd drop-in /etc/systemd/system/opennms.service.d/malloc-arena.conf, both from the pool sweep. Provisiond entirely at stock: scan pool corePoolSize 10, maxPoolSize Integer.MAX_VALUE. Latency injection: tc qdisc netem delay 75ms 25ms on netsim enp6s19, so 50-100 ms uniform per SNMP PDU. GC logging was NOT configured on either JVM and was enabled at runtime with jcmd VM.log before arming; the gc.log files under hosts/*/jvm/*/ were pulled by hand because the skill derives GC log paths from the JVM command line. Core enp6s20 (Kafka) pcap ring wrapped: its oldest packet is 08:52:47Z against a 08:48:44Z start, so that interface covers the last ~22.5 min. Minion rings did not wrap at this fleet size. This is the second attempt: the first (results-attempt1, 07:17-08:00Z) lost its procfs pollers when an interrupted stop was retried; that bug is fixed in benchmark-capture da70e4e. NOT IN GIT: the heap raise, the netsim resize to 4 vCPU / 8 GiB and nl6 v0.28.0 are live-only.
